The Cincinnati Cyclones announced that they’ve re-signed forward Max Helgeson for the 2026-27 season. The upcoming season marks Helgeson’s first full professional season.

ChooseHockey Skates

Go ad-free with ITR+

Helgeson, 25, joined the Cyclones last season after finishing his collegiate career. Last season, Helgeson played in 15 games with the Cyclones, recording four assists, four points, and four penalty minutes.

Prior to going pro, Helgeson played four seasons of NCAA Division I  hockey. During his time at the NCAA level, Helgeson played at the University of Alaska Anchorage and Miami University. Throughout his time playing with the Seawolves, he recorded 33 goals and 35 assists for 68 points in 95 games. During his last two seasons with the Seawolves, he served as alternate captain. Helgeson then transferred to Miami University, where he finished his NCAA career. While playing with the RedHawks, he recorded ten goals and ten assists for 20 points in 36 games.

Go ad-free with ITR+

Before playing at the NCAA level, Helgeson played one season in the ACHA at Lindenwood University. In 16 games, he recorded eleven goals, twelve assists, and 23 points. During the 2021-22 season, he recorded one goal and two assists in four playoff games and claimed the ACHA National Championship.

Helgeson’s NAHL Career

The Anchorage, Alaska, native played two seasons of junior hockey in the NAHL. During his time in the NAHL, he played with the Janesville Jets, Jamestown Rebels, and Kenai River Brown Bears. While playing with the Jets, he recorded one assist in two games. During his time with the Rebels, he recorded two assists in eight games. Throughout Max Helgeson’s time with the Brown Bears, he played in 95 games, recording 37 goals, 48 assists, and 85 points. During the 2020-21 season, he recorded five goals and three assists in nine playoff games and served as alternate captain.
